subject: Audit & access log export scenarios — retention windows and formats
messages:
From: Jared Lawson <jared.lawson@acmehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit/access logs: export formats and retention windows

Hi Priya,

We’re putting together a scope for an upcoming security assessment and need to understand Redwood’s current capabilities around audit and access logs. A few specific questions:

- What are the default retention windows for audit events vs. access logs on Hosted accounts?
- Can we request bulk exports (full history) of audit logs? If so, what formats do you support (NDJSON/CSV/Parquet/syslog)?
- Do you support push-to-S3 (customer bucket) or only pull exports via Console/API?
- How do you handle data residency for exported payloads (we’re US-based but have EU nodes for other workloads)?
- For deletions/retention enforcement, what evidence do you provide (audit trail, hashes) to demonstrate a record was purged?

Also please share any standard SLA or turn-around times for large export requests (e.g., 30M events). Attaching our internal checklist would be helpful but I’ll send that separately.

Thanks,
Jared
Security Ops — Acme Health
--Attachment: acme_export_checklist.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 14KB)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Lawson <jared.lawson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@finserv.io>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit/access logs: export formats and retention windows

Hi Jared — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details + next steps below.

Quick summary:
- Hosted defaults: access/activity logs = 30 days; audit events (user/admin actions, config changes) = 90 days.
- Enterprise (reserved/dedicated) can extend retention up to 365 days; Private deployments can retain per customer policy (including indefinite).
- Export formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON), CSV (flat view), Parquet (recommended for large exports), and syslog stream for near-real-time forwarding.
- Delivery: we support both push-to-S3 (customer-owned bucket with configurable prefix and encryption) and Console/API downloads. For extremely large archives we offer multipart S3 delivery.
- Residency: exports honor the account’s residency settings. If the account is US-resident, exports originate from US regions. For cross-region requests we provide transfer controls and explicit confirmation.
- Deletion evidence: we provide an audit trail showing the delete action (who/when/request id) plus optional cryptographic hash snapshots on request for legal/forensic needs.

What I need from you to scope:
1) Which log classes are required (audit events, access logs, API request logs, KV cache traces)?
2) Timeframe (start/end dates or rolling window).
3) Preferred format and destination (e.g., Parquet -> s3://acme-redwood-exports/2026-09).
4) Desired SLA (e.g., 48-hour turnaround for up to 50M lines).

We can turn around a standard export for up to 30 days worth of events from Hosted in ~24–48 hours; larger archival exports are scheduled and quoted (typically 3–7 business days depending on size and region). For your compliance review we can include the audit_export_matrix_v2.csv (shows column mappings) and our audit playbook PDF. I’ll loop in our compliance engineer internally to confirm S3 delivery options.

Next steps: can you confirm items 1–3 above? I’ll draft a formal export request template and estimated timing.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Audit/access logs: export formats and retention windows

Hey all — quick confirm from infra/compliance:

- S3 push: Yes, we support push to customer-owned S3 buckets. We use server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) on our side if requested and support delivering encrypted objects to your bucket; alternatively we can hand off a presigned multipart upload if you prefer to deposit directly.
- Format guidance: For large-scale exports we recommend Parquet (better compression + schema preservation). NDJSON is fine for ad-hoc smaller sets or streaming.
- Retention defaults: Hosted -> access logs 30d, audit events 90d. Enterprise/Dedicated extension -> up to 365d. Private -> configured by the customer; we have customers keeping multi-year archives.
- Export window: Hosted accounts can request exports up to 365 days back (subject to retention and availability). If requested data exceeds retention (e.g., you want 2+ years from Hosted), we’ll need an archive request — typically Approved by Compliance and scheduled as a special project.
- Chain of custody: We can compute SHA-256 hashes for exported files and include a manifest with timestamps and request IDs.

I’ve attached the export matrix that maps event types to output columns and estimated sizes per 1M events.

Neha Kapoor
Compliance Engineer — Redwood Inference
